Chapter 3. The Mind of the Assassin and the Web of Conspiracy.
While the president was doing everything he could to help heal a divided nation, there was another man moving through the city, driven by a very different purpose.
He was an actor—someone you might call charming, even magnetic, at least in the right company. But underneath that, he carried a heavy resentment. In his eyes, the president was a tyrant, someone who’d destroyed the world he loved.
And he wasn’t the only one who felt this way. He found others, each wrestling with their own anger and fears. They met in secret corners, sharing their frustrations, whispering about what could be done. The city buzzed with rumors, but hardly anyone guessed just how deep their plot ran.
Inside the assassin’s mind, pride and bitterness twisted together with a frightening sense of desperation. He actually believed he was on a noble mission—certain that taking the president’s life would somehow save the country. So, he watched the president’s every move, searching for weaknesses, waiting for that perfect opportunity.
The group’s plans grew bigger and bolder as days went by. Kidnapping, disrupting the government, striking a blow for the South—they talked it all through. But as the war neared its end, their desperation only deepened. The president’s hopeful ideas about reconciliation felt like a threat to everything they still believed in. Eventually, they convinced themselves that only his death could change the future.
So, the conspirators spread out across the city, gathering intel, making preparations. Some watched the president’s home. Others followed his carriage, noting every routine. Each person played a part—some brought weapons, others shared information, a few just offered support.
The assassin’s sense of destiny was unshakeable. He pictured himself as a hero—a man whose actions would be remembered. He rehearsed his plan again and again, playing out that decisive moment in his mind. He honestly believed the country would thank him for it, that his name would be celebrated.
Yet, most people were completely unaware of the danger lurking nearby. The city bustled with celebrations, rumors, and the daily grind of rebuilding. The president’s security was light, and hardly anyone believed he was in real danger.
As the day of the assassination drew closer, tension built among the conspirators. Some started to have doubts—what if it all went wrong? But the assassin pressed on, convinced he was doing the right thing. He believed history would vindicate him, that his actions would change the course of the nation.
In those final hours, he moved with absolute focus. He checked his weapons, reviewed the plan, and steeled himself for what was coming. In his mind, the fate of the country rested entirely in his hands.
The web of conspiracy was tight, but never perfect. There were mistakes. Some conspirators hesitated. But not the assassin. His determination never wavered. He was ready, absolutely convinced that his moment had finally arrived.
